title: Growing Welsh onion
subtitle: A perennial spring onion that divides and expands without ever needing replanting.
excerpt: Welsh onion is a hardy perennial that grows in clumps and produces spring onion-like stems all year. It is never truly dormant in a UK winter and can be harvested in every month of the year. Divide clumps every two to three years to keep it productive.
sourceNotes: Cultivation notes from Joy Larkcom, Oriental Vegetables (1991). Plants For A Future database (pfaf.org). UK hardiness data widely documented in horticultural literature.

glossaryTerms.definition: Propagating a perennial by splitting the whole plant into smaller sections, each with roots attached. Done every two to four years to prevent overcrowding, maintain vigour, and create new plants. Welsh onion, sorrel, and lovage all benefit from periodic clump division.

content.text: Welsh onion is a perennial onion that produces hollow, spring-onion-like stems throughout the year. Unlike most onions, it does not form a single bulb. Instead it grows in expanding clumps that can be harvested at any time. It is one of the most productive perennial vegetables in a UK kitchen garden.

Sow seed in pots in March to April or August to September. Germination is fast in warm conditions. Plant out 20 to 30 cm apart in groups of three to five seedlings per station. Alternatively, buy a pot-grown plant and divide it in spring or autumn.

Cut individual stems at the base as needed. The remaining stems in the clump continue to grow. You can also pull individual bulbs from the outer edge of the clump. In winter the stems are thinner and less vigorous, but present all year in a sheltered UK garden.
Every two to three years, lift the whole clump in spring or autumn and divide it into smaller sections by
. Replant the sections 20 cm apart. This keeps the plants productive and stops the centre becoming woody and unproductive.

attrs.title: Welsh onion in containers
attrs.body: Welsh onion grows well in a large pot or half-barrel. It is one of the most productive container perennials because it provides a harvest every month of the year. Use a deep container (at least 25 cm) and a compost-rich mix. Water in summer dry spells. Divide and repot every two years to maintain vigour.
